title: Daily Market Digest: October 15, 2026
subtitle: Tech Sell-Off Continues Amid Inflation Fears, Dow Edges Up

items.headline: Inflation Fears and AI Debt Concerns Drive Tech Sell-Off, Broader Market Mixed
items.summary: U.S. equities saw a mixed performance today as persistent inflation data and rising anxieties over AI infrastructure financing weighed heavily on the technology sector. While the Nasdaq experienced significant declines, the Dow Jones Industrial Average managed to eke out gains, indicating a rotation into more defensive sectors. Investor sentiment remains cautious following a hotter-than-expected Producer Price Index (PPI) and continued hawkish signals from the Federal Reserve regarding potential interest rate hikes. Not financial advice.

items.headline: Ericsson Surges on Strong Q3 Earnings
items.summary: Ericsson's shares climbed after the telecom equipment maker reported robust Q3 revenue of SEK59.5B, surpassing analyst expectations, alongside higher-than-anticipated GAAP EPS of SEK1.77.

items.headline: Penske Automotive Group Rises
items.summary: Penske Automotive Group saw its shares advance significantly today.

items.headline: Eli Lilly & Co. Gains Momentum
items.summary: Healthcare giant Eli Lilly and Co. experienced a notable increase in its stock price, contributing to the defensive sector's strength.

items.headline: Rocket Lab Tumbles on Neutron Rocket Delay
items.summary: Shares of Rocket Lab fell sharply after the company announced a delay in the inaugural launch of its new Neutron rocket until next year, raising concerns about development costs and revenue deferrals.

items.headline: Dell Technologies Slumps on Downgrade
items.summary: Dell Technologies' stock declined after Barclays downgraded the hardware and server manufacturer to Equal Weight from Overweight, exacerbating a broader technology sector retreat.

items.headline: AMD Falls Amid Semiconductor Sector Worries
items.summary: Advanced Micro Devices ($AMD) experienced a significant decline, reflecting broader concerns and a sell-off within the semiconductor industry.

items.headline: Hotter-Than-Expected Inflation Revives Fed Rate Hike Bets
items.summary: U.S. inflation data released this week, including a 3.7% Consumer Price Index (CPI) for September and a 6.3% rise in the Producer Price Index (PPI), has fueled expectations of further interest rate hikes by the Federal Reserve. This data, surpassing economists' forecasts, has particularly impacted growth-oriented sectors like technology.

items.headline: AI-Linked Stocks Face Deepening Rout Amid Debt Concerns
items.summary: A global sell-off in artificial intelligence (AI) and semiconductor stocks intensified, driven by fears of potential hits to AI investments from higher interest rates and concerns over the financing of AI infrastructure. Companies like SK Hynix, CoreWeave, and TSMC saw significant drops, despite some reporting strong earnings.

items.headline: Defensive Sectors Lead as Investors Seek Safety
items.summary: Amid the tech downturn and inflation worries, investors rotated into traditionally defensive sectors. Healthcare and Consumer Staples showed resilience, with the Health Care Select Sector SPDR Fund ($XLV) gaining 2.42% and the Materials Select Sector SPDR Fund ($XLB) rising 1.73%.

items.headline: Major Companies Report Q3 Earnings; Mixed Results Noted
items.summary: Several major companies released their third-quarter earnings today. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. ($TSM) reported record profits but saw its stock fall due to broader market sentiment. Ericsson ($ERIC) beat revenue and EPS estimates, while ManpowerGroup ($MAN) reported increased net earnings and revenues. U.S. Bancorp ($USB), PNC Financial Services ($PNC), Charles Schwab ($SCHW), and Alcoa ($AA) were also scheduled to report.
